card_summary: The proliferation of video walls in live production environments signals a growing need for real-time, low-latency signal transport. To meet this demand, engineers should prioritize ST 2110-based solutions, leveraging NMOS for device discovery and control. However, the complexity of these systems can lead to signal integrity issues, making genlock and frame-accuracy a critical concern. In practice, this means that engineering teams must carefully balance the benefits of low-latency transport with the need for robust signal integrity. The trade-off here is between the precision of JPEG XS compression and the potential for increased latency, which can compromise the real-time nature of live video walls. To mitigate this risk, teams should opt for solutions that incorporate multiple transport protocols, such as SRT and RIST, to ensure reliable and low-latency signal transport.

Why Broadcasters Must Prioritize Low-Latency Signal Transport for Real-Time Decisions

As the media industry grapples with the sheer volume of content being produced and consumed, broadcasters are facing unprecedented pressure to make real-time decisions that drive audience engagement and revenue growth. The increasing complexity of live signal transport, coupled with the need for low-latency delivery, is forcing broadcasters to rethink their infrastructure and workflows. With the rise of IP-based signal transport, the stakes are higher than ever before, and the wrong choice can have far-reaching consequences.

What This Development Actually Means

Haivision has announced a major breakthrough in video wall technology, enabling real-time decision-making for broadcasters and content creators. The company's solution leverages the power of ST 2110, a suite of standards for professional media over IP, to transport high-quality video and audio signals with unprecedented low latency. This marks a significant shift in the industry, as broadcasters can now rely on a single, unified platform for live signal transport, eliminating the need for multiple, disparate systems.

This development responds to the growing demand for real-time decision-making in live production, driven by the proliferation of social media, online streaming, and the need for instant feedback from audiences. With the ability to transport high-quality video and audio signals in real-time, broadcasters can now make informed decisions that drive engagement and revenue growth.

Why It Matters for Broadcast Operations

The adoption of ST 2110-based video wall technology will have far-reaching implications for broadcast operations, particularly in terms of CapEx and OpEx. With a single, unified platform for live signal transport, broadcasters can eliminate the need for multiple, disparate systems, reducing hardware rack footprint and simplifying signal routing. This will also enable broadcasters to take advantage of lower latency than satellite or fibre-based solutions, reducing the risk of delays and errors. For example, Matrox ConvertIP gateways, Riedel MediorNet, and Harmonic VOS360 are all well-positioned to support this shift, offering high-quality, low-latency signal transport solutions that meet the demands of live production.

Impact by Stakeholder

  • Regional and national broadcasters: Will need to budget for ST 2110-based video wall technology to take advantage of low-latency signal transport and simplified signal routing. This will enable them to reduce transmission costs and improve overall efficiency.
  • OTT and streaming platforms: Will need to adapt their delivery workflows to accommodate the increased demand for low-latency content. This may involve implementing ABR ladders with reduced latency, optimizing CDN costs per GB, and simplifying SSAI complexity.
